content.title: Celestial Event Route Rewrite | New Light, Obstacle Birth, Carrier Adaptation
content.summary: An atmospheric glider crosses ice rings created by a second aurora core. Preserve the five causal invariants and terminal proof while replacing every source-specific surface.

quick_start.input_format: One route and carrier exist before the world event. + A visible global event changes the route conditions. + New obstacles emerge from that event rather than random cuts. + Carrier direction and recurring landmarks preserve geography. + The exit proves adaptation while the changed world persists.
quick_start.recommended_input: Establish one original survey glider crossing a calm upper atmosphere beneath a single pale moon. The bent clouds condense into a chain of rotating ice rings across the same forward route. Exit the last ring into open sky while both aurora cores and the changed cloud route remain visible.
required_anchors: One route and carrier exist before the world event.
A visible global event changes the route conditions.
Carrier direction and recurring landmarks preserve geography.
The exit proves adaptation while the changed world persists.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: An atmospheric glider crosses ice rings created by a second aurora core. Preserve the five causal invariants and terminal proof while replacing every source-specific surface.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.
